subject: Optimize Toolkit pilot packaging + initial pricing questions
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Optimize Toolkit pilot packaging + kickoff

Hi Amy / Peter —

Thanks again for a great intro yesterday. As discussed, I wanted to put a short summary and proposed next steps for a 6–8 week Optimize Toolkit pilot focused on reducing token spend for your customer-facing extraction pipelines. High-level:

- Objective: 30–50% unit-cost reduction on production inference by combining batching, prefix/KV caching, and model quantization with Redwood-managed fallbacks.
- Scope: 3 inference routes (document parsing, conversational re-rank, embeddings) + a short eval suite (provided by you or we can use our baseline prompts).
- Outputs: technical runbook, pilot credits, quantization recommendation, and SOW for production rollout.

I've attached a one-pager with the proposed packaging and three sample commitment tiers (small pilot, standard pilot, pilot+rollout delta). Before we lock anything down, two quick asks so we can get Connor and Marcus lined up:

1) Can you confirm typical average sequence length and QPS during peak for the parsing route (ballpark is fine)?
2) Any constraints on model variants we should avoid (e.g., strict accuracy retention required vs. acceptable <5% quality delta)?

Proposed next steps: internal technical kickoff (Connor) + commercial alignment (Marcus + me). I'm available Tue/Wed next week for a 30-min sync.

Best,
Kimberly Park

Hi Kimberly — thanks for the note. Good summary. A few clarifications from our side so we can scope the pilot properly:

- Parsing route: avg seq len ~620 tokens, bursts up to ~1,800 for long documents. Typical QPS on peak: 6–8 sustained, spikes to ~15 for short windows.
- Re-rank: mostly short context (<=120 tokens), QPS 30–40.
- Embeddings: batch jobs at night, no hard SLA.
- Quality: for parsing we need >95% field-extraction accuracy relative to our golden set; <3% degradation is the hard limit. For re-rank we're more tolerant up to ~5% depending on rubric.

On pricing: we'd like to understand how pilot credits map to production commit tiers, and what's the floor for discounts on a first-year committed contract. Procurement will likely require a simple SOW and a 60-day payment term.

Happy to take your calendar invite for next week.

Best,
Amy
Product Lead — Data Platform, Pinebridge AI
amy@pinebridge.ai
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Optimize Toolkit pilot packaging + kickoff

Amy — quick technical readout based on your numbers and our internal pilot templates. TL;DR: we can meet your accuracy targets and still deliver meaningful cost savings if we scope quantization conservatively on parsing and be more aggressive on lower-sensitivity routes. Details: 

1) Parsing (avg 620, spikes 1,800):
   - Approach: use prefix KV-caching for repeated doc headers + dynamic batching for tail-latency control. Target batching window = 12–25ms to avoid increasing p50 beyond your SLOs.
   - Quantization: start with INT8 dynamic range on the primary model; run a closed A/B on 5k golden examples to validate <3% accuracy impact. If that passes, we can test GPTQ-lite for another ~3–4% savings but only in a canary subset.
   - Expected savings: 25–40% token-cost reduction if prefix caching hits >25% of requests.

2) Re-rank (<=120 tokens):
   - Approach: small-batch (up to 16) synchronous batching + lightweight quantization (INT8). Because the context is short, quantization is low-risk and can yield 30–45% compute reduction.

3) Embeddings (batch jobs):
   - Approach: schedule deduped batched runs in off-peak windows; large-batch quantized runs (INT8 or 4-bit if acceptable) yield the largest $$ savings.

Operational notes:
- We'll instrument token-level cost dashboards and failure-rate alerts and gate any production rollout behind quality regression alarms.
- For the A/B runs we'll need ~2–3 business days to integrate your golden set and run the automated comparisons.

I'll prep a short technical runbook and sample eval pipeline ahead of the kickoff.

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Pilot pricing options and discount scenarios

Amy / team — following Connor's technical plan, attaching a simple pricing worksheet with three commercial paths:

- Option A (Discovery Pilot - no commit): 8-week pilot, $0 upfront (we provide $12k in pilot credits), measured outcomes report. No long-term discount commitment.
- Option B (Pilot + 6mo production commit): $40k one-time pilot + 6-mo minimum commit (committed $/month). We offer a 12% first-year volume discount and up to 10% additional credit if you commit to upfront payment.
- Option C (Pilot + annual commit): $80k pilot credit offset + 18% first-year discount, tiered unit pricing driven by monthly token bands.

Concessions we can consider for a strategic reference customer: pilot credits increase by 25% and an additional 5% discount on year one for use cases that go live within 120 days. Any longer-term discounts need to be tied to commit bands.

Attachments: pilot_pricing_options.xlsx, SOW_draft_Pinebridge.pdf

Notes on NRR/SLAs: standard Dedicated pricing and SLA options are available once usage crosses the committed throughput thresholds; Marcus can share a separate Dedicated pricing sheet if you want isolation and tighter latency SLOs.

Marcus Lin
Head of Commercial Programs, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Amy / Procurement team — thanks for the quick responses. To make progress on contracting and technical kickoff, here's what we'd like to lock in this week: 

1) Choose a commercial path: Option B (Pilot + 6mo commit) or Option C (Pilot + annual commit). If you want to proceed with Option B, we can offer the reference concession (25% extra pilot credits) if Pinebridge agrees to a public case study after pilot completion.

2) Procurement asks: if 60-day net is acceptable, we'll circulate the attached SOW and a redline-friendly contract. Please confirm billing contact and PO process.

3) Technical kickoff: Connor will run the A/B integration — can you send the golden-set samples (anonymized) and a short sample of high-length docs by EOD Thu so we can schedule the evaluation run next week?

I'll drop a HubSpot deal link and a DocuSign SOW template once you confirm Option B vs C.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.
